findings.title: --flusher-processes accepts zero and negative values
findings.body: The new --flusher-processes option accepts any integer. In SpanFlusher, 0 is treated as unset because it uses `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `--flusher-processes 0` unexpectedly starts one heavy spawned Sentry/Kafka-producer process per assigned shard. Negative values flow into `min()` and shard modulo indexing, which can raise a KeyError or start no flusher workers during consumer construction. Validate this as a positive integer, for example with click.IntRange(min=1) and equivalent validation in SpanFlusher/ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.

findings.title: Comma-joined shard list corrupts metrics tags
findings.body: When one flusher process handles multiple shards, which is the normal case when flusher_processes is smaller than the shard count and always the case for the CLI default of 1, `shard_tag` becomes a value such as `0,1,2`. Passing that comma-containing value as a StatsD/DogStatsD tag makes the backend parse it as `shard:0` plus stray tags `1` and `2`, so the produce, wait-produce, and segment-size metrics cannot be correctly attributed by shard. Emit these metrics per flushed segment/shard or otherwise use a single sanitized shard tag value.

findings.title: Multi-shard flusher test never flushes any spans
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit creates four shards mapped to two flusher processes, but it only asserts process counts and then joins without submitting spans or advancing the flush clock. The existing basic test covers only one shard/process, so the central new behavior—a shared process correctly flushing, producing, and completing segments for multiple shards, without drops or duplicates—is untested. Add an end-to-end test that stores spans across several shards with fewer flusher processes than shards and asserts the produced segments for each shard.
